library(tidyverse)

Let's explore Maryland elections, power outages and electric vehicle data and make some maps!

## Questions

**Q1.** Q1. In 2022, Maryland elected the state's first two African-American statewide office holders: Wes Moore as governor and Anthony Brown as attorney general. You want to compare the two's electoral performances. Using the `md_statewide_county.csv` file in the data folder, calculate the total number of votes for both the governor's race and the attorney general's race, then percentages for both Moore and Brown *based on the total of their respective contests*. Then calculate the difference between their percentages.

Get the geometry for Maryland's counties using tigris and, joining that dataframe to your results dataframe, make a county-level map of the differences between Moore and Brown's percentages. What is the story here, and what is the county with the most interesting results?

**A1.**

I wouldnt say its that interesting how much more Worcester County pulled for Moore, esp as Moore has beena. huge funding sponsor and support of tourism groups that have spent a ton of money in recent years trying to make Ocean City a cool boardwalk spot!

```{r}
maryland_mega_statewide <- read_csv("data/md_statewide_county.csv") |> clean_names()
outages_across <- read_csv("data/county_outages_march2023.csv") |> clean_names()
ev_data <- read_csv("data/ev_2020_2023.csv") |> clean_names()

counties <- counties()
md_counties <- counties |> filter(STATEFP == "24")

moore_vs_brown_percents <- maryland_mega_statewide |>
  mutate(governor_total = cox + moore + lashar + wallace + harding + sefcik + gov_writein,
         ag_total = peroutka + brown + ag_writein,
         pct_moore = (moore / governor_total) * 100,
         pct_brown = (brown / ag_total) * 100,
         difference = pct_moore - pct_brown,
         geoid = as.character(geoid)) |>
  select(geoid, county, pct_moore, pct_brown, difference)

moore_vs_brown_percents |> arrange(desc(difference))

county_shapes_with_moore_brown <- md_counties |>
  left_join(moore_vs_brown_percents, join_by(GEOID == geoid))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = county_shapes_with_moore_brown, aes(fill = difference)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option = "magma") +
  labs(title = "Support for Moore vs Brown", fill = "Gap between Moore and Brown support")
```

**Q2.** Make a county-level map to explore the number of customers impacted by power outages in Maryland from last March. Load the `county_outages_march2023.csv` file in the data folder and calculate a rate of customers with outages per 10,000 total customers for each county. Then join that dataframe to your Maryland counties dataframe you made in Q1 and create a county-level map of the results; you may need to tweak the fill scale to make the distinctions clearer.

What's the potential story here? Given access to other months' outage data, what would your next steps be in reporting a story?

**A2.**

```{r}

md_counties_with_join_name <- md_counties |>
  mutate(county_join = case_when(NAMELSAD == "Baltimore city" ~ "Baltimore City", .default = NAME))

outage_map_data <- md_counties_with_join_name |>
  left_join(outages_across |> mutate(rate_per_10000 = (outage_customers / total_customers) * 10000), join_by(county_join == county))

outage_map_data |> filter(is.na(rate_per_10000)) |> nrow()

ggplot() + geom_sf(data = outage_map_data, aes(fill = rate_per_10000)) + theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option = "magma", trans = "log") +
  labs(title = "Washington and Frederick continue to lead in power outages of all MD counties", fill = "Customers without power per 10,000")

census_api_key("keyyyyyy api hereee")


```

**Q3.** You've been assigned a story about the use of electric vehicles in Maryland and you want to make a map of the prevalence of electric vehicles in each county. Load the `ev_2020_2023.csv` file, which has the number of electric and hybrid vehicles per county from July 2020 and March 2023 and calculate a percentage change for each county (remember, that's `new-old/old`). Using the Maryland counties dataframe you made for Q1, make a county map showing the percentage change. What counties stand out to you? What questions do you have about the changes you're seeing?

**Caroline County has a really interesting boost here! I am curious for the very obvious question of "why" lol!**

Next, use tidycensus to retrieve county population data for Maryland from 2021 (you did this in the pre_lab) and join it to your vehicles dataframe. HINT: you may not need to join it on the county name, and you should already have the geometry!

Then, calculate a per capita rate of electric & hybrid vehicles using the March 2023 figure and the population estimate. You will need to choose the "per capita" value.

Finally, make a second county map showing the per capita rate. What counties stand out on this map? How is it different from the first one you made?

**A3. \
This one is a bit more predictable... the highest wealth in md (near dc) has the most EVs proportionally. MoCo stands out the most!**

```{r}

county_populations_2021 <- get_acs(geography = "county", variables = c(population = "B01001_001"), year = 2021, state = "MD") |>
  select(GEOID, population = estimate)

ev_map_data <- md_counties_with_join_name |>
  left_join(ev_data, join_by(county_join == county)) |>
  left_join(county_populations_2021, join_by(GEOID)) |>
  mutate(pct_change = ((march_2023 - july_2020) / july_2020) * 100, ev_per_1000 = (march_2023 / population) * 1000)

ev_map_data |> filter(is.na(pct_change)) |> nrow()

ggplot() + geom_sf(data = ev_map_data, aes(fill = pct_change)) + theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option = "magma") +
  labs(title = "Caroline County sees huge increase in number of EVs", fill = "% change in EVs from 2020 to 2023")

ggplot() + geom_sf(data = ev_map_data, aes(fill = ev_per_1000)) + theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(option = "magma") +
  labs(title = "MoCO has highest amount of electric vehicles per population", fill = "EVs per 1,000 people",)
```
